tools.name: mailboxes_list
tools.title: List mailboxes
tools.description: List the connected mailboxes that answer, each by the name a tool's mailbox input takes, and the tools its provider does not offer.

tools.name: messages_list
tools.title: Search a mailbox
tools.description: Search one connected mailbox in its own provider's query language, Gmail's or Outlook's.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

q.description: A Gmail mailbox reads Gmail's search operators: from:, to:, cc:, subject:, is:unread, is:starred, in:sent, has:attachment, filename:pdf, after:2026/01/31, before:, newer_than:7d, larger:5M, OR, -word and ( ). An Outlook mailbox reads Microsoft's keyword query language - from:, to:, cc:, subject:, body:, received:, hasAttachments:true, plain words and quoted phrases, AND, OR and NOT in capitals - and never a filter expression such as isRead eq false. A few distinctive words, with OR between alternatives, miss less than a copied subject line or sentence.

by.description: message, the default, answers each matching message; thread answers each matching thread with every message in it.

view.description: summary, the default, carries each message's subject and snippet; headers leaves both out.

pageToken.description: The nextPageToken of the page before, asked with the same q and by. Outlook pages threads by their matching messages, so a thread can recur on a later page.

tools.name: messages_list_all_mailboxes
tools.title: Search every mailbox
tools.description: Search every mailbox you have connected in one call. The answer names the mailbox each result came from, names any mailbox it could not search, and is merged newest first by when each message arrived, a thread by its newest.

q.description: A Gmail mailbox reads Gmail's search operators: from:, to:, cc:, subject:, is:unread, is:starred, in:sent, has:attachment, filename:pdf, after:2026/01/31, before:, newer_than:7d, larger:5M, OR, -word and ( ). An Outlook mailbox reads Microsoft's keyword query language - from:, to:, cc:, subject:, body:, received:, hasAttachments:true, plain words and quoted phrases, AND, OR and NOT in capitals - and never a filter expression such as isRead eq false. A few distinctive words, with OR between alternatives, miss less than a copied subject line or sentence. Where the mailboxes are of different providers only from:, to:, subject:, plain words and quoted phrases are read alike, with no AND, OR or NOT.

by.description: message, the default, answers each matching message; thread answers each matching thread with every message in it.

view.description: summary, the default, carries each message's subject and snippet; headers leaves both out.

maxResults.description: How many results to take from each mailbox.

tools.name: messages_get
tools.title: Read a message
tools.description: Read one message in a connected mailbox, with its headers and its body.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

id.description: The message's id, as a search or a thread read answered it, or a draft's own id.

view.description: full, the default, carries each message's text and attachments; summary leaves those out; headers leaves out the subject and snippet too.

tools.name: drafts_update
tools.title: Edit a draft
tools.description: Change a draft in a connected mailbox. A field the call leaves out stays as the draft has it.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

id.description: The id a draft tool answered, or the draftId a search or a read answered.

to.description: Who the message is addressed to.

bcc.description: Who to blind-copy. The other recipients are not told.

body.description: The whole message text, a reply's quote included. Given without html, the draft becomes plain text.

html.description: The whole message as HTML, for formatting; given without body, its plain-text version is read from it. An Outlook mailbox keeps only the HTML and writes the plain version from it.

attachments.description: Files to carry, each held by a connected mailbox of the draft's own provider or written out. Named, they replace the ones it holds, and an empty list removes them all. An Outlook draft takes on the new files before it gives up the old, so a replacement stopped midway is reported and may leave both. An Outlook draft sent while it is rewritten may lose its old files from the sent copy.

mailbox.description: The mailbox holding the message the file is in, of the same provider as the one written from.

attachmentId.description: An attachment id, as a message read named it.

tools.name: drafts_reply
tools.title: Draft a reply
tools.description: Compose a reply to a message as a draft, inside the thread it answers and quoting it below the reply: to whoever wrote it, or with replyAll to everyone on it. Nothing leaves the mailbox until the draft is sent.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

html.description: The message as HTML, for formatting; body stays its plain-text version. An Outlook mailbox keeps only the HTML and writes the plain version from it.

to.description: Who the reply goes to, instead of whoever wrote the message and, with replyAll, those it was sent to.

cc.description: Who to copy, instead of those replyAll copies.

replyAll.description: Also address everyone the message was sent to and copied - never its blind copies, never this mailbox.

bcc.description: Who to blind-copy. The other recipients are not told.

attachments.description: Files to carry: one held by a connected mailbox of the draft's own provider, or content you write out.

mailbox.description: The mailbox holding the message the file is in, of the same provider as the one written from.

attachmentId.description: An attachment id, as a message read named it.

tools.name: messages_send
tools.title: Send a message
tools.description: Compose a new message in a connected mailbox and send it in one call. Call this only when the person asked for this message to go; when they asked to prepare one, draft it instead. A request id already spent sends nothing again: the answer says whether that send went or may have gone.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

to.description: Who the message is addressed to.

bcc.description: Who to blind-copy. The other recipients are not told.

html.description: The message as HTML, for formatting; body stays its plain-text version. An Outlook mailbox keeps only the HTML and writes the plain version from it.

attachments.description: Files to carry: one held by a connected mailbox of the message's own provider, or content you write out.

mailbox.description: The mailbox holding the message the file is in, of the same provider as the one written from.

attachmentId.description: An attachment id, as a message read named it.

requestId.description: Your own id for this send, new for every message. One whose send went or may have gone sends nothing again.

tools.name: drafts_send
tools.title: Send a draft
tools.description: Send a draft. It leaves the mailbox and consumes the draft. Only a draft is sent: a message already sent or received is refused, and nothing leaves. Call this only when the person asked for this message to go; when they asked to prepare one, draft it instead. A request id already spent sends nothing again: the answer says whether that send went or may have gone.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

id.description: The id a draft tool answered, or the draftId a search or a read answered.

requestId.description: Your own id for this send, new for every message. One whose send went or may have gone sends nothing again.

tools.name: messages_reply
tools.title: Reply to a message
tools.description: Reply to a message, inside its own thread and quoting it below the reply: to whoever wrote it, or with replyAll to everyone on it. Call this only when the person asked for this message to go; when they asked to prepare one, draft it instead. A request id already spent sends nothing again: the answer says whether that send went or may have gone.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

html.description: The message as HTML, for formatting; body stays its plain-text version. An Outlook mailbox keeps only the HTML and writes the plain version from it.

to.description: Who the reply goes to, instead of whoever wrote the message and, with replyAll, those it was sent to.

cc.description: Who to copy, instead of those replyAll copies.

replyAll.description: Also address everyone the message was sent to and copied - never its blind copies, never this mailbox.

requestId.description: Your own id for this send, new for every message. One whose send went or may have gone sends nothing again.

tools.name: messages_forward
tools.title: Forward a message
tools.description: Forward one message to the addresses you name, with the files it carries, inside the thread it already sits in. Only the provider's own limit applies to what it carries. Call this only when the person asked for this message to go; when they asked to prepare one, draft it instead. A request id already spent sends nothing again: the answer says whether that send went or may have gone.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

to.description: Who the forward is addressed to.

note.description: Your own words, above the message forwarded.

html.description: Your own words as HTML, for formatting; note stays their plain-text version. An Outlook mailbox keeps only the HTML and writes the plain version from it.

requestId.description: Your own id for this send, new for every message. One whose send went or may have gone sends nothing again.

tools.name: labels_list
tools.title: List labels
tools.description: List the labels a connected mailbox holds, by the id each is applied by.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

tools.name: labels_create
tools.title: Create a label
tools.description: Create a label in a connected mailbox and answer the id it is applied by. In a Gmail mailbox a / nests it under the label before it, made first where missing; in an Outlook mailbox a / is just a character.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

tools.name: labels_update
tools.title: Edit a label
tools.description: Rename a label, recolour it, or both. The id comes from labels_list. An Outlook mailbox's categories are its labels, and Microsoft lets one take only a new colour.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

tools.name: labels_delete
tools.title: Delete a label
tools.description: Delete one label, by its id from labels_list. No message is deleted: in a Gmail mailbox the label comes off every message; an Outlook mailbox's category leaves its list, and the messages that carried it keep its name.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

tools.name: threads_modify
tools.title: Label a thread
tools.description: Apply and remove labels on one thread, or one message of it - an Outlook mailbox's categories are its labels. The ids come from labels_list. Adding SPAM junks it, and taking SPAM off brings it back to the inbox. In a Gmail mailbox adding TRASH bins it too; an Outlook mailbox takes no other id.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

id.description: The threadId a search or a read answered, or with scope message the message's id.

scope.description: thread, the default, acts on the whole thread; message acts on that one message alone.

tools.name: messages_attachments_get
tools.title: Read an attachment
tools.description: Read one attachment of a message. The answer is what it says, as plain text; with as original it is the file itself, base64. messages_get and threads_get name a message's attachments and their sizes. Either answer names the address the original is served at whole, to a GET carrying this same credential.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's name or its email address.

messageId.description: The message's id, as a search or a read answered it.

id.description: An attachment id, as a message read named it.

as.description: text, the default: what the file says. original: the file itself, byte for byte.

continuation.description: Where the words resume, as the last part read named it. The original always comes whole.
